svg.aria-label: How to write 喜: 12 strokes · 11 pen lifts · 12 movements
svg.title: Writing 喜
svg.desc: 12 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 喜 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 喜.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%96%9C.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喜, and they descend the character in four bands: medians 1–3 the 士 at the top, medians 4–6 a 口, medians 7–8 the short pair beneath it, median 9 the single widest horizontal in the character, and medians 10–12 the closing 口. Top before bottom throughout, and each 口 is built left side, joined top-and-right, closing floor — the order the reader already writes. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the two joined corners and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's ninth stroke runs slightly wider than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.
